---
title: "Firm-pair probabilities and report-card blocks"
subtitle: "5.4 · after Kline, Rose and Walters (2024), Figure 5A"
description: "Comparison of isolated-pair thresholds with the relations in KRW's coherent cards."
---

Each cell contains the posterior probability that the row firm's contact gap exceeds the column firm's gap.
The matrix includes every ordered pair and the diagonal. Thresholding identifies directions that would minimise
loss for each pair considered separately. The archived card's grade blocks identify the statements in a coherent
report. Comparing the two reveals high-probability directions withheld within grades and additional directions
stated between grades. The probability scale is retained throughout; darker blue represents greater support for
the row-above-column direction rather than a larger error probability.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **All direction probabilities.** The Blues legend is labelled “Pr(row truly higher)”. A darker cell means a
  larger direction probability; it does not mean a larger error. Arrow keys move through the complete matrix,
  and each cell names both firms and the card’s relation.
- **Above the threshold.** At λ .25, the corresponding withholding cost is τ .20. The strict pairwise rule
  would state 1,575 pairs whose favored direction has probability above .80. Other cells fade, while the grey
  diagonal continues to mark self-comparisons.
- **Add the card blocks.** The card withholds 575 bright pairs inside its blocks. It also states 324 pairs whose
  error exceeds τ. These are consequences of fitting directions into one coherent report, not a cap on grades.
- **λ .50 blocks.** The threshold admits 2,994 pairs. Of these, 49 are withheld by the card; 545 stated pairs have
  error above the current τ. Varying the reward changes both the threshold and the selected archived card.
- **Gender blocks.** The target is the signed male-name contact advantage. Negative gaps favor
  female-named applicants. Both row-above-column directions retain this signed orientation.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
Grid cards were computed with KRW’s code under archived probabilities and solver tolerances. Their evaluations
here use the released postrank probabilities and supply no new optimality certificate. Race’s baseline card is
Figure 7; gender is Figure 14 (§VIII). Figures 5A and 6 are in §V.E, and Figure 10A is in §VI.B.
